1.title: Borealis Order 1 - pneumatics, electronics
rows: PRESSURE SIDE - tanks, rear manifold, main valve and in valves (200 psi)
Air tank 6 L / 1.6 gal, 200 psi, 1/4 NPT, aluminum (your pick)
Two, 12 L: left and right over the front wheels. The CAD test-fit found no room for a third alongside them; 9-15 shots at 120 ft per 150-200 psi charge with a fast top valve, 6-10 with a slow one
Relief valve 200 psi, 1/4 NPT male, ASME, ring pull, brass, 2-pack (Loner ST25-1A200, B0F4QP9CG2)
Tank zone (rear manifold; its ring at the rear panel is the hand dump), the valve cross, and the cross after each in valve on the chassis (its ring is that chamber's bleed)
Pressure transducer 0-300 psi, 0.5-4.5 V, 5 V, 1/8 NPT, stainless, with plug cable (pick "1set-300PSI")

One part number for all three: the tank, and one per chamber on the chassis cross after its in valve (Brophy Borealis compact gun), so no sensor wires cross the pivot. Fill in short pulses and read between them: the hose reads a little high while air is flowing. +$1.99 shipping
Quick disconnects: 1/4 NPT female M-style couplers, brass, 300 psi, 5-pack (RUBY.Q B0BPXT6V2F)

The 4 interior quick disconnects: each tank line into the rear manifold (2), each chassis cross to its chamber hose (2). Couplers have the shut-off, so they go on the supply side (1 spare); none on the main valve line (Micah 2026-11-12: the main valve shuts it)
QD plugs + fill plug: 1/4 NPT FEMALE-thread M-style plugs, brass, 10 pcs (ZKZX B081F9J3VF, pick 'Female NPT')
5 used: the fill plug outside the rear panel (on the 2-1/2 in nipple; your universal couplers snap on) and one per interior QD. Still an open plug, so the check valve behind it stays
Fill check valve, 304 stainless, 1/4 NPT male x male (your AliExpress pick)

Behind the panel, between the female elbow and rear manifold cross B (straight in, 2026-11-12). Holds the tanks shut when the hose comes off (the plug is an open pipe). No pressure rating listed, so leak-test it at 200 psi with soapy water
In valves: GOGO GPG-M03 2/2 NC direct-acting 12 V DC, G1/4 (BSPP), 2.5 mm, 0-35 bar (option 1/4", DC12V, 2.5mm 35bar)

One in valve per chamber, metering it against the transducer on its chassis cross; they hold tank pressure all session. G1/4 ports: a G1/4 x 1/4 NPT adapter with a bonded seal in each (rows below). Flow arrow toward the chamber; soap-test at 200 psi
Adapters: G1/4 BSPP male x 1/4 NPT male hex nipple, 304 stainless (pick "G1/4 BSPP / 1/4 NPT / Male to male")
Both ports of both in valves: inlet to its QD plug, outlet to its chassis cross. They take the place of 4 close nipples. Bonded seal on the G1/4 side, sealant on the NPT side only
Bonded seals: self-centering NBR, 14 mm (fits G1/4), 20 pcs (pick "14mm")
One under each adapter's hex at the in valve ports (4 of 20): G1/4 is a parallel thread, so it seals on the face, not the thread

5 used, one spare (Micah 2026-11-12: one 6-pack is cheaper than two 3-packs): two for the rear manifold, the valve cross, and one on the chassis right after each in valve: its chamber's transducer, relief and hose out (moved off the gun, Brophy Borealis)
1/4 NPT brass close nipple, 5-pack, 250 psi (FLOFLEX B0CRVX12WC)

2 used (CAD count, Brophy Borealis): one joining the rear manifold's two crosses, one between cross A and the main ball valve. The in valves' ports take the G1/4 adapters, which screw straight into the valve cross and the chamber crosses, so one pack is enough (3 spare)
1/4 NPT brass 90 deg elbow, FNPT x FNPT, 2-pack (ChillWaves B0B7544Y62)
Fill line behind the panel: the nipple in one side, the male x male check valve in the other (1 spare)
1/4 NPT brass street elbow 90 deg, MNPT x FNPT, 2 pcs (CX Wonderland B0BCZFCFQ7)
1 used: the tank relief off the bottom of rear manifold cross B, turned to the rear panel (1 spare)
1/4 NPT plug, 304 stainless, hex socket, 10 pcs (Neprift B0H6X8VCSZ)

Every open port (rev D.2 audit): up to 3 spare bungs per tank (photos show 3-4 ports; one is the outlet) = 6 of 10. The rear manifold, valve cross and chassis crosses have no open port (2026-11-12: the manifold is two real crosses now)
1/4 NPT male x 1/8 NPT female hex bushing, brass, 5 pcs (Litoexpe B0BFW3Q864)
DOT nylon air-brake tube 1/4 in OD, SAE J844 PA12, 35 ft, with cutter (Boeray B0CYFWGSYS)
Every air line, including the two service loops to the gun (about 15 ft used)
DOT push-to-connect 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT male, straight, 10-pack (Boeray)
14 used: both halves of the 4 quick disconnects (8), rear manifold (2), main valve, valve cross, and the hose out of each chassis cross (2). One row now: the quick-disconnect row was the same listing
DOT push-to-connect swivel elbow 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT, 5-pack (Boeray)
4 used: the two tank outlets and the two chamber inlets (in the weld-on bungs, pointing at the pivot); 1 spare
Pipe thread sealant, RectorSeal T Plus 2 (B0002YPAFY)
Main valve: 1/4 NPT brass ball valve, FNPT x FNPT, 600 WOG, 2-pack (B0FKHG6VVT)
Manual tank shut-off (rev C.3): open for a session, closed for transport and before working on the gun; handle at the rear panel
1/4 NPT brass nipple 2-1/2 in, male x male, 2-pack (Legines B0747L5XQZ)

Through the rear panel: the female plug outside, the female elbow inside on the rear manifold's axis (2026-11-12: the fill check valve now screws straight into cross B, so the nipple reaches further in). A check valve's 10 mm male end is too short to cross the panel itself
GUN - welded 3 in pipe chambers (Brophy Borealis): top 1.56 L, bottom 1.32 L, both on HSV04 valves to 190 psi; 36 in barrels
Firing valves: U.S. Solid USS-HSV04, 1 in NPT, 12 V DC, NC, pilot-operated, 1-50 bar (725 psi), PTFE seal (Amazon B0BSNHJ4WQ)
One per cannon (rev D.2: the bottom one too, so both run to full tank pressure, capped at 190 under the 200 psi reliefs)
Chamber end plates: 3/8 in A36 hot-rolled steel, 4 x 16 in (B08C2FD1QH)

Waterjet four 3.5 in discs, flush with the pipe: each front disc gets a 1.33 in hole for its outlet nipple, the back discs are blank. Bevel the pipe ends 37.5 deg and weld all the way through. 3/8 in is about twice the thickness 200 psi needs
Chambers: 3 in Sch 40 steel pipe, plain end, 24 in (A500, B0FLF5VJMG)

Cut 12.9 in for the top chamber (about 1.56 L) and 10.9 in for the bottom (about 1.32 L). Water-test each welded chamber to 300 psi for 10 minutes before it holds air (borrow a hand test pump and a 0-600 psi gauge). A steel-yard drop works too if it's cheaper
Chamber inlets: 1/4 NPT female steel weld-on step bung, 2-pack (B0H6VR9N6R)
One per chamber on the pipe wall about 1 in behind the front plate, facing the pivot side, so the inlet and outlet are at the same end. A swivel push-to-connect elbow screws in
1 in NPT close nipple (1-1/2 in), seamless steel, Sch 80, ASTM A106, 300 psi (Grainger-approved B007IBN8T4)
Each firing valve to its breech adapter (the chamber side is now the welded nipple in the next row)
Chamber outlets: 1 in x 4 in black steel pipe nipple (LDR 300 1X4, B0002YV7GU)
Cut in half: each cut end is welded through its chamber's front plate, and the HSV04 screws onto the threaded end
Cuts the 1 in NPT threads through the two aluminium breech pucks. Each puck is JB Welded into the back of its barrel, and the whole barrel screws onto its firing valve's nipple
MOSFET switch module 5-36 V 15 A, 3.3-20 V trigger, 10-pack (B0GGHY11RL)

6 used in this order: firing valves (2), in valves (2), and the contactor coil twice in series (one channel for the main controller, one for the safety node). The light bar and smoke get their own pack in Order 2
Barrels: clear extruded polycarbonate tube 3.00 in OD x 2.75 ID x 1/8 wall x 36 in (K-mac B09NLCGBWB)
Two 36 in barrels as they come. Three 3/8 in smoke holes each, leaning 45 deg to the muzzle; drill them after the barrel is screwed home so they face the other barrel
Breech pucks: 6061 flat bar 1 in x 4 in x 8 in, T6511 (B0CCGN9HSQ, pick the length)

Two pucks, 2.5D on the CNC: a 3 in x 1/4 in flange the barrel butts on and a 2.74 in x 3/4 in spigot JB Welded inside it, 1 in NPT tapped straight through (the tap is on this list). Barrel + puck is then one piece: it slides into the gun core from the front and screws onto the firing valve nipple
ELEVATION - 312 rpm FTC motor on a Spark MAX (backdrives when off), pot for the angle
goBILDA 16T pinion to the printed 112T pivot pulley (CAD loop is exactly 750 mm)
CONTROLS, FAILSAFE + POWER - back bottom bay
Anderson SB50 flush-mount bracket + dust cover kit
Standby charge / shore-power port, bottom of the rear panel (a stash SB50 housing goes in it)
Main controller: Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT, ESP32-P4 + ESP32-C6 (B0FDWZ6KWT)

One board does it all (rev D.2.1): web UI and WebSocket on 2.4 GHz WiFi 6 (the C6 on the board), valves and chamber metering, elevation loop, every LED strip, audio mixing out of its own speaker amp into the siren amp, MIPI camera later, lidar on a UART, the PDH contactor and both battery relays. 5 V from the logic rail on its SH1.0 power header

#1: the three pressure transducers + the 5 V reference. #2: battery A, battery B, the bus and the PDH volts, so the battery relays compare the two packs to a few mV. Both on I2C to the main controller (its own ADC only reads the pot)

12 of 16 used: drive PWM to the 4 Falcons and the elevation Spark MAX, fog heater (2), pump, blower, light bar, both battery relays. Valves, LED data and the contactor stay on the board's own pins (timing and safety). OE is pulled up and held low by the controller, so a reset or crash turns every output off
12 V 40 A relay with pre-wired socket
Valve arm relay (valve rail, fed from the PDH); flyback diode on the coil. The two fog relays are in Order 2
Relay coils from 3.3 V logic: the valve arm relay, both battery relays and the two fog relays (0.15 A coils; COM to +12 V clamps the flyback)
Contactor + battery relays: 12 V 200 A continuous duty, isolated coil, 4-pin (B0D97PSZBB)

1: the power cut-off between the main breaker and the PDH. Its coil runs through the rear E-stop, the safety node's switch and the main controller's MOSFET in series, so any one of them kills drive, valves, LEDs, audio and fog. 2: one in each battery's + lead, between its SB50 and the shared bus; the controller keeps only the fuller pack connected until the other is within 0.3 V, so a fresh battery never dumps 20-40 A into a flat one
Battery relay bypass: 4.7 ohm 5 W cement resistor, 10-pack (B0FG25KG8C)
One across each battery relay (2 used): feeds the logic rail and boots the controller while both relays are open (power-up, or a dead controller), and trickle-balances the packs at well under 1 A
Logic supply: 5 V 5 A buck-boost module, 3.6-32 V in (pick "5V")
Always-on 5 V logic rail, tapped ahead of the contactor: main controller (its 5 V header), safety node, every sensor
Rear panel: one contact in the contactor coil (kills the PDH), the other in the valve arm relay coil; + the handheld remote
Panel-mount USB-C extension, 30 cm, IP67, male to female, USB 2.0 (pick "0.3m")
USB to the main controller through the rear panel (30 cm reaches the controller on the bellypan)
Safety remote: TP4056 Type-C 18650 charger board with protection (pick "TP4056 Module TYPE-C", "1PCS") + a stash 18650 cell

Remote power, charged over USB-C, inside your custom printed remote case: OUT+ through a slide switch to the C3 SuperMini's 5V pin (its regulator holds 3.3 V down to about 3.4 V on the cell), OUT- to GND. Charge with the remote switched off, and never plug USB into the C3 with the cell connected
RIVETS - first order (Micah, 2026-11-11: "if we order rivets, they should be in the first order")
Rivets: 3/16 in aluminium blind rivets, dome head, 3/16 x 1/4 (6-4, 0.188-0.250 in grip), 100 pcs (B07KPQM2TZ)

About 138 used (one pack: you have plenty more): every waterjet bracket that isn't countersunk (inboard plates, arm knees, top corner gussets, tower plates) into its tube. A 1/8 in plate on a 1/16 in tube wall is 0.188 in, the bottom of this grip
Rivets: 3/16 in aluminium countersunk blind rivets, 120 deg, 3/16 x 1/4 (0.126-0.250 in grip), 50 pcs (B0B33RF991)

About 100 used: the side plates (the wheels run right beside them), the bottom corner gussets (the underglow bracket runs right under them) and the bellypan (a smooth underside). Countersink those holes 120 deg after the waterjet
DRIVE - old 9 in mecanum wheels on Falcon 500s (owned / stash)
HTD 5M 15 mm drive belt, 140T (700 mm), rubber, 1 pc (uxcell B0DSQWZBVR)
One per wheel: Falcon 12T to the wheel's 116T (9.67:1), as the CAD's drive is drawn. If the old 9 in wheels end up on a different pulley, re-pick the length (the 12T stays)
ALREADY HAVE - owned or FRC stash, $0, nothing to buy
Gun cradle plates: 1/8 in aluminium sheet (stash), 2, CNC router

The gun's two side plates (chevron + turret wheel), 490 x 226 mm each, about 0.7 kg. Every hole is 4.5 mm for an M4 and has a part behind it: 14 side screws into inserts in the saddles, chamber caps and gun core halves, 3 into the add-on rail's T-nuts, the hub's 4 (left plate) or the ring pulley's 6 standoffs (right plate), plus the 1/2 in hex for the pivot stub

Printed gun parts (PETG): 2 gun core halves, 2 chamber saddles, 4 chamber caps, 2 chamber end covers, axle hub, axle spacer, 112T ring pulley (its 6 standoff posts printed on, an M4 insert in each), 16T pinion, smoke collar, muzzle ring

Gun core halves (left / right): each is one side's valve blocks, half the breech block and half the mantlet; 2 x M4 x 12 across the split clamp both barrels onto their spigots, then 6 x M4 x 8 through each side plate. Saddles and caps hold the chambers (the rear set is V-shaped like the plates' back). 5 walls, 40% gyroid
goBILDA 5203-2402-0019 Yellow Jacket 19.2:1 (312 rpm), 8 mm REX (owned)
16T -> 112T belt to the ring pulley on the gun's right cradle plate (7:1, about 45 rpm free at the gun, 16.7 N*m stall)
Drives the goBILDA in brushed mode from PWM
Gun angle on the end of the left pivot stub through a printed coupler (it passes through the tower plate's hole), to the main controller's own ADC on 3.3 V (both ADS1115s are full)
Printed board trays (3DP): one under each board on the bellypan, 6 mm standoff posts with heat-staked pegs

Seven trays (controller, safety node, PCA9685, both ADS1115s, drivers board, logic supply): each board drops onto four printed pegs that a soldering iron mushrooms over (no screws, nothing conductive under the board); each tray takes 2 x M4 x 12 up through the bellypan into M4 inserts
One per side on its own slide-out sled, each through its own battery relay (below)
REV PDH + ATO breakers, 120 A main breaker, SB50s, wire and lugs

Main power: the 120 A breaker is the robot's on / off switch, on the rear panel beside the E-stop (its trip button and reset lever through a 42 mm hole). The E-stop only drops the contactor; the logic rail stays up until the breaker is off
1: safety node (ESP-NOW to the remote; holds the PDH contactor in only while the remote and the main controller are alive). 2: spare
Inline ATO fuse holder + 5 A fuse
Logic tap, right after the main breaker
Resistors and caps (kit): ADC dividers, pull-downs, RC filters

Three transducers (10k/15k), battery A, battery B, bus and PDH volts (39k/10k), 100k pull-downs so a cut sensor wire reads as a fault, the speaker tap, a 330 ohm series resistor on each LED data line (no level shifter)
Safety remote: ESP32-C3 SuperMini (one of yours)
Handheld E-stop (the second mushroom above) plus a status LED that shows the link is up; ESP-NOW to the safety node
One per wheel, plain PWM from the main controller (no gate: the contactor is the cut-off)
Old 9 in mecanum wheels (owned, for now)
Stand-ins for the printed 10 in vector wheels (Micah, 2026-11-04); belts and hubs depend on how they mount
2 per wheel axle (inner + outer rail), 4 at the pivot
1/2 in hex shaft: 4 wheel axles (6-3/8 in) + 2 pivot stubs

Live axles tapped 10-32 both ends, each ending inside the outer rail in its bearing (the end screw and washer go in through a 14 mm hole in the rail's outer wall, which the bumper covers: no holes in the bumper); one steel stub per cradle plate on the pivot axis (2.7 in left, 2.2 in right), tapped 1/4-20 both ends: a 1/4-20 button head and washer inside the cradle plate and one outside the outer bearing keep each stub from sliding (stash hardware)

notes.B6: 200 psi, 1/4 NPT female bungs (photos: 2 along the side, one in an end); it ships with welded feet the CAD saddles ignore. $56.60 list; a $46.81 welcome deal shows for new shoppers. 4.9 stars, 90 sold (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B7: ASME, 200 psi set, 1/4 MNPT, stainless pull ring, 178 cfm; was McMaster 48435K72 4 x $6.67 (Amazon/Ali only, Micah 2026-11-10). Only 8 packs left (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B8: Universal 5 V sender, 30-1000 psi options, connector included; 3K+ sold, 4.8 stars, $10.69 (2026-11-09, L). Was the FUSCH on Amazon at $17.69 each (B0CRQWKDNC). Check the 0.5-4.5 V output on the option page before ordering
notes.B9: 300 psi working; with the plugs below replaces the $27.98 Lnrueg 45-pc kit (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B10: Kenzo's pick was the Male NPT option, which doesn't thread onto the nipples; no psi on the listing (the couplers are the 300 psi parts) (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B11: Male on both ends (listing photo), not FNPT x MNPT as an older note hoped. The listing gives no pressure rating (an older note's '250 psi, brass' was a different valve), so leak-test it at 200 psi before it holds air. Fit it with the flow arrow pointing in (2026-11-06, L; note corrected 2026-11-11)
notes.B12: GOGO Automatic Company Ltd. (GOGO's own store), 290 sold. $18.22 each + $12.01 shipping split over the two, logged-in price. Brass, NBR seal, DIN plug; body 40 x 26 mm, 76 mm tall, 82 mm long with the plug, 2 x M5 x 8 mounting holes underneath. Coil power not listed (likely 15-20 W: fine on its 15 A MOSFET channel). Replaces the Aignep 02F ($41.36 at Hose Warehouse, 2 mm), Micah's pick (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B13: China Pneumatic Factory Store, 386 sold. $1.77 each + $5.69 shipping split over the four, logged-in price (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B14: SOREKARA, 317 sold, 5.0 stars. $2.78 + $1.99 shipping; the $1.09 it shows is a new-shopper price (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B16: 250 psi rated, 1/4 MNPT both ends; was Legines $7.99 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B17: 1/4 NPT female both ends, barstock brass, 1,200 psi; now $6.39, only 8 left (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B18: Brass, 1/4 MNPT x 1/4 FNPT; no psi on the listing (the old 5-pack had none either); was $11.99 for 5 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B19: 8 used, 2 spare; one 10-pack instead of two brass 5-packs ($15.98) (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B20: 1200 psi rated; was McMaster 9151K91 3 x $2.16 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B21: 500 psi working, 4.35 mm ID; 10 ft more than the old 25 ft roll for less (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B22: 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT male, 250 psi, SAE J1131 + J844, brass; 18 left (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B23: 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT male, 250 psi, SAE J1131 (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B24: Skip it if you have pipe dope or PTFE tape (Home Depot's $4.25 isn't one of your sellers) (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B25: Free shipping; 12 sold, 5 stars. Was $8.99 on Amazon (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B26: You don't have one (Micah, 2026-11-11), so it's a buy: heavy-duty brass, female both ends, 600 WOG (over 4 x the 190 psi it sees); 4.5 stars. One spare (2026-11-11, L)
notes.B27: Same Legines line as the 1-1/2 in it replaces (that one listed 1200 psi; this one lists no psi). In stock (2026-11-12, L). One spare
notes.B29: In stock, one version only. Thread is listed as NPT / G (a dual thread, no option to pick), so true NPT is NOT confirmed: test-fit a 1 in NPT nipple before trusting it at 190 psi. Cv 11.67, 25 mm, PTFE seal, junction box. Opening time unpublished: bench-test before cutting barrels (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B30: Four 3.5 in discs fit on the 4 x 16 in bar with room for the kerf. Replaces the four MSI chamber couplings ($111.80) now the chambers are welded. Plain steel has no part rating: the welded chamber is the pressure part, water-tested to 300 psi before it holds air (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B31: Plain-end A500, 0.216 in wall; the listing states no psi. 12.9 + 10.9 in leaves 0.2 in of the 24: make it one bandsaw cut, and if the pipe arrives short or out of square take both chambers down 1/16 in. The 16 in ($28.52) + 12 in ($20.24) lengths cost $8.28 more and leave room to face the ends (2026-11-10 review, L)
notes.B32: 1/4-18 NPT, collar OD 24.8 mm x 16.5 mm (the CAD draws the 22 mm AC Performance one: drill the pipe to this one's step); only 15 left (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B33: Sch 80: same 1.315 in OD (no CAD change), bore 24.3 mm vs 26.6 mm, about the HSV04's own orifice; the only Sch 40 ones on Amazon are 150 psi decorative pipe. Was McMaster 44615K416 2 x $3.13 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B35: Borrow one if the shop has it. 4.6 stars (2026-11-02, S)
notes.B36: Triggers from 3.3 V, so the controller drives them directly (no buffer). Flyback diode across each valve coil; was two 6-packs $10.98 (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B37: Same tube as McMaster 8585K38 ($66.05), free delivery; only 2 left. No pressure rating (none published at McMaster either); clamp it. Not acrylic: it shatters (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B38: [UNVERIFIED price: Amazon listing not readable, estimate; Zoro sells 1 x 4 x 6 at $26.19] Not the 1 x 3 bar: no clean-up round the 3 in flange (Micah 2026-11-12: no aluminium stock, 2.5D only)
notes.B40: 9 mm to match goBILDA's HTD pulleys (AliExpress only has 10 mm); was $8.99 at WCP (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B43: Micah picked it 2026-11-09 over the WTDKP4C5-S1 ($29.29) for the USB plugs: 4 USB-A + 2 USB-C, RJ45 (PoE header), a 40-pin Pi-style header with 28 GPIO (takes Pi HATs), ES8311 codec + NS4150B 2 W speaker amp + mic, speaker included. 2.4 GHz only, so the access point runs 2.4 GHz. Sold by UeeKKoo, 3.6 stars (10); Waveshare store $19.99 + shipping, AliExpress from $27.89 (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B44: Settled call: ESP32 ADCs are too nonlinear for pressure. Two for the price of the single (B0FLPZMQJY, $7.99); 5 stars (3), 50+ bought last month (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B45: The 28 header pins can't take all ~38 D.2 signals; this frees 12. One PWM frequency for all 16 (about 200 Hz suits the Falcons, Spark MAX and light bar; on/off loads use full-on/full-off). 4.5 stars (104), 200+ bought last month (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B46: 4-pin option; 211 sold. Replaces the Nilight 5-pack ($12.14) and the Gebildet 2-pack ($7.99) (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B48: 200 A continuous, 4-pin; only 8 left (3 needed); was $12.99 B07T48QKQB (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B49: Under 1 W each in the worst case: a fresh and a flat pack, one relay open, full drive load. 5 stars (7) (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B50: The row had no link: this is the 3.6-32 V to 5 V / 9 V / 12 V 5 A module, $2.67, 4.8 stars, 413 sold; pick the 5V option. Short-circuit, over-temperature and TVS protection; holds 5 V down to 3.6 V in, so a drive sag can't reset the controllers. Was the PM02 at $13.30 (2026-11-10 review, L)
notes.B51: Pick the 2 NC option; 180 sold, 4.9 stars. Was $13.99 each (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B52: 600+ sold; USB 2.0 is all the ESP32-P4 needs to program. Was the 10 cm one ($2.06): too short (Micah). Check the panel hole size on the listing before cutting the acrylic (2026-11-11, L)
notes.B53: 1,000+ sold, free shipping, overcharge / over-discharge / short protection. Replaces the $3.29 battery shield: no 5 V boost needed (Micah: just the board) (2026-11-11, L)
notes.B55: Fastenere 6-4, open end, 5052 body. Checked the listing (2026-11-11, L)
notes.B56: Metal Magery, 100% aluminium; 16 left when checked (2026-11-11, L)
notes.B58: 4.4 stars (131), $8.90 each (10% off, typically $9.89) (2026-11-11, L). Added so the CAD and the parts list match (Micah)
notes.B60: From your aluminium (Micah, 2026-11-11). One DXF per plate in docs/glacis/gun_plates/ (mm). The only CNC router parts: 490 x 226 mm is too big for the 12 x 12 in waterjet. The pockets' inside corners are 4 mm radius, so a 1/4 in end mill or smaller reaches them; drill or helix the 4.5 mm holes
notes.B61: Filament is the PETG row. Every part fits a 250 mm bed (a core half is 242 x 197 x 74 mm, printed outer face down)
notes.B62: Owned: Micah has every goBILDA motor (2026-11-04)
notes.B65: Filament is the PETG row (2026-11-11, L)
notes.B67: Owned / Standard FRC stash part; buy only if the stash is out

2.title: Borealis Order 2 - materials, LEDs, smoke, audio
rows: AUDIO - two siren speakers in the front corners (replaces the horn)
Siren speaker 200 W, 8 ohm, 121-130 dB, aluminium, 5.7 x 5.5 x 2.3 in (Xprite B01DMSR4L4)
One high in each front-side corner, in a printed cup, aimed 45 deg out and 30 deg up; its L foot bolts through the cup
TPA3255 2 x 300 W class-D amp board, 19-50 V DC, 122 x 73 x 30 mm
One channel per speaker; about 70 W each into 8 ohm on 33 V
1200 W 20 A boost converter, 8-60 V in, 12-80 V out (set to 33 V; pick the "1200W 20A" option)

Feeds the amp from a 40 A PDH channel. At 33 V the amp tops out near 70 W per speaker (about 2 dB under 100 W), so the board stays under the 15 A where the listing asks for extra cooling. The $1.09 price on the listing is a one-time new-shopper offer
SMOKE - custom 12 V fogger (one 200 W core, room for a second), barrel collar, front and rear trail vents
Fog heater core 12 V 200 W, cast heat exchanger 97 x 32 x 36 mm
The fogger: about 17.5 A on its own 30 A PDH channel
Fog fluid pump: Kamoer NKP 12 V peristaltic, 70 mL/min
Feeds the core from the printed tank (a second one comes with a second core)
Core temperature to the main controller (SPI); hold 220-240 C, firmware cut at 245 C
1-Wire on one controller pin: fogger box by the printed tray (heater off at 70 C), electronics shelf, battery bay; 2 spare
12 V 5015 blower, 2-pack (Diann B09W5N73BD, dual ball bearing)
Pushes the fog from the cores into the splitter and down the three tubes
Fog fluid, water-based, medium density, 1 gal (B0DF5RCGJX)
Fills the printed tank about 9 times
Silicone tube 3/4 in ID x 1 in OD, 1/8 in wall, 9.84 ft, food grade, -60 to 240 C (Quickun B091SP66Z9, pick the 3/4 x 1 in size)

The gun's smoke line: splitter, up through the well floor, into the gun core, then dead centre between the two barrels to the smoke collar. 3/4 in ID (Micah: go bigger): about a fifth of the 1/2 in line's pressure loss, so the blower actually pushes fog through it. The barrels are only 25 mm apart, so it squishes to an oval there: every printed hole it passes through is oblong. Some fog always condenses in the line; a wide, short, smooth run with no low sag loses the least, and insulating it barely helps
MOSFET switch module 5-36 V 15 A, 6 pcs with heat sinks (MTDELE B0D9VWWLCB)
5 used: light bar (PWM), fog heater (2), fog pump, blower (moved from Order 1)
12 V 40 A relay with pre-wired socket
One per fog core (the second for a second core later); flyback diode on every coil (moved from Order 1)
FRAME + BODY - box tube, printed frame, recessed acrylic
Heat-set inserts M4 x 4, brass, OD 5 mm, 100 pcs (M4X4X5mm option): every M4 insert

About 102 used, so two packs (spares for the ones that go in crooked): panel clips (40), speaker cups (8), the gun (30: 8 in the chamber saddles' sides, 8 in the chamber caps' sides, 12 in the gun core halves' sides, 2 for the core's clamp screws), the in-well rails' screws (10, in the deck's well-edge member), the front light bar rails' screws (4), the 112T ring's 6 printed posts (one at each post's plate end). The holes stay as drawn (4.7 mm, 6.5 deep; 4.6 deep at the 12 tight clips): the insert sits at the top and the screw tip runs on into the plastic below
M4 x 12 button head, 304 stainless, 100 pcs

Frame-joint cross screws (40, self-tapping into the tenon's pilot), standoffs, the pivot bearing blocks down onto the in-well rails (4, into T-nuts), the elevation motor bracket up into the right rail (2, into T-nuts), the left axle hub (4, through its flange and the plate into nylocs), the gun core's 2 clamp screws (across the split between the barrels, into inserts)
M4 x 8 button head, 304 stainless, 100 pcs (B0DKXNTRTW)

About 122: panel clips (28, plus the 12 short ones with a screw cut to 6 mm), speaker cups (8), gun rails (6, through the cradle plates into T-nuts), the light bar's 2 bracket feet, the front rails (4), the 112T ring's 6 printed posts (6, from inside the right cradle plate into the posts' inserts), and the gun's side screws through the cradle plates into inserts (28: 8 into the chamber saddles, 8 into the chamber caps, 12 into the gun core halves)
Foam tape 1/4 in x 1/16 in, white, 2 x 33 ft (Yotache B0CCKJ2ZTV)

About 13 m round every panel's acrylic ledge, so the clips clamp the panels instead of letting them rattle (the rebate is 0.7 mm deeper for it). White, so it doesn't read as a dark line through the frosted acrylic
42 used: 13 in the frame (8 in tabs on the side walls' inner faces, 5 in the end walls), 13 in the posts' feet, 16 in the bumper corner brackets
RAILS - 20x20 T-slot rails (Brophy Borealis): two inside the gun well, two on the gun, two across the front light bar hole
M4 drop-in T-nuts for 20-series (6 mm slot), M4 x 10 x 6, 50 pcs

14 used: 3 per gun rail, 1 under each light bar bracket foot, 2 under each pivot bearing block (in the in-well rail's top slot), 2 for the elevation motor bracket (the right rail's bottom slot). Drop in from the side after the rail is placed
M4 x 30 button head screws, ISO 7380, black 10.9 steel, 30 pcs
10 used: through holes CNC'd across the in-well rails' core (8 mm head access from the gun well) and the tower plates into inserts in the deck's well-edge member
LIGHTS - panel loops, glowing frame, underglow, front light bar
WS2812B LED strip 5 mm wide, 2020 LEDs, 100 LED/m, 5 m

7.6 m: one piece per frame member (the front and rear bottom members have no tunnel: a jumper wire runs round them), LEDs out, bent the easy way up into the feed slot at each end and soldered to the next at the slot mouth
WS2812B LED strip 10 mm, 60 LED/m, 5 m, black PCB, IP30
11.2 m: one closed loop per panel on its window wall, centred 25 mm behind the acrylic, LEDs aimed across the panel; 2.5 m of underglow under the bumpers from the rest of the third reel
Front light bar: Zmoon 12 in single-row LED bar, 72 W spot/flood combo, 12/24 V (your pick)

In a plain hole at the bottom of the front slant (Brophy Borealis: from the bumper to 4.5 in above it, open at the bottom, no liner), standing on the lower of two 20x20 rails across the hole on its own end brackets, aimed straight ahead; the upper rail is free for sensors. The main controller switches it (and can PWM-dim it) through a MOSFET channel; about 6 A at 12 V
LEDs only, on a PDH channel, so they go dark with the PDH
3M double-sided tape, heavy duty, 0.39 in x 15.4 ft, black, 2-pack (Xguider B0GBVMRXM5, pick 0.39")

Holds the underglow strip on its printed brackets' 45 deg face (the strip's centre just under the bumper's bottom edge), and the 14 brackets onto the rails' bottom wall (no rivnuts): about 4 m used of 9.4 m
3-pin LED wire, 22 AWG stranded tinned copper, 3 colours, 100 ft (AOTOINK B08JTZKN4M)

Every strip's 5 V / data / GND run back to the main LED board, and the jumpers between panels (40 ft is the minimum, 100 ft leaves spare). 22 AWG is enough: the worst plug carries one panel loop, about 1.2 A at the 20% white cap, about 0.2 V drop over a 1.5 m run. The frame runs get their 5 V injected at the frame nodes, so their cable only carries data and a little current
Servo extension leads, JR/Futaba 3-pin, male to female, 15 cm, 22 AWG, 20 pcs (OliYin B07QJSWNFM)

Cut each lead in half: 20 plug pigtails for the strip ends and 20 socket pigtails for the panel-to-panel outputs. Five board outputs: left panels (front, front side L, battery door L, deck strip L), right panels (rear, front side R, battery door R, deck strip R), left frame, right frame, underglow. Every panel has its own plug in and plug out, so any panel unplugs on its own and every LED stays individually addressable (one data line per chain, nothing in parallel). About 11 plugs and 6 sockets used
BUMPERS - FRC style ring, slides off downward
6 used: x -80, 0, 80 on each side strip, driven in from the foam side, so the screw from inside the rail pulls the flange into the 1x6. With 3/4 in wood the screws become your 1-1/4 in #10-32s
Bumper foam: GoTo Foam 5 x 24 x 24 in, 43 ILD firm, 1.8 lb density (your pick, B07SDNP781)

Replaces the pool noodles: cut strips 5 in tall x 1-13/16 in deep x 24 in (1-13/16 in so the 3/16 in gap between the ring and the chassis keeps the robot 27.75 in wide). The ring needs about 120 in (two 27.75 in ends, two 32.2 in sides): 6 strips of the 12 a block gives
Canvas: HYVAKUPPA 12 oz cotton duck, 59 x 72 in (2 yards), white (B0H753QCN1, pick "White", "2 Yards")
Bumper covers wrapped round the foam and the 1x6 backing: cut down the middle, two 29.5 x 72 in pieces give 144 in of wrap for the 120 in ring
PETG filament, white, 4 kg (iSANMATE HF B0FXG1TGYQ)

Every printed part, about 6.5 kg sliced: the body frame about 3 kg, the other body prints (clips, posts, brackets, speaker cups) about 2 kg, and about 1.5 kg for the gun (core halves, saddles, caps, end covers, hub, ring pulley), the electronics shelf, battery sleds and smoke parts. One 4 kg bundle plus your 3 kg makes 7 kg, about 0.5 kg for failed prints
ALREADY HAVE - owned or FRC stash, $0, nothing to buy
Speaker tap: 2 x 1k + 2 x 10 nF low-pass + 1 uF cap (from the kit)

Replaces the PCM5102A: one wire of the board's speaker output (SPK+) through a two-stage 1k/10 nF low-pass and a 1 uF cap into the TPA3255's input (L and R together). Volume and mix are set in software; the amp's gain pot sets the top end
Cup lines each corner notch, 4 x M4 x 8 through its walls into the frame; the speaker's foot bolts through it; grille: 3 walls, no top/bottom layers, 12% gyroid
Silicone tube 3 mm ID x 5 mm OD (per metre)
Tank -> pumps -> core inlets (zip-tied on the 2.5 mm tubes)
M5 aluminium standoffs (stash): 4 under the fog heater bracket
Hold the fog heater's aluminium bracket off the smoke tray. Metal, not printed: the core runs at 220-240 C
Splitter to the front and rear vents (both down through the bellypan)
Printed smoke parts: tray, 400 mL tank, 1-to-3 splitter, one-piece smoke collar, front and rear vents (PETG/ASA)
Ducts, vents and the barrel collar
M4 nylon-insert lock nuts, 304 stainless, 100 pcs (B0BHQMBRFX)
The left axle hub's 4 bolts (M4 x 12, through its 3 mm flange and the cradle plate)
Frosted acrylic 1/8 in (owned): 8 panels (the front is one U-shaped sheet round the light bar hole)
Recessed in the printed frame, held by corner clips; cut 1 mm under the rebate outline all round
Printed body frame: 50 pieces incl. two front cheeks, 58 tapered tenons (40 cross-screwed, 18 glued), 40 corner clips, 14 underglow brackets, 13 frame mount posts, 4 bumper corner brackets (PETG)
Holds the panels; a strip tunnel down every member (the frame glows); each window wall chamfers from the acrylic ledge to its LED strip

1/2 in x 35: frame to posts (13, up from each post's outer pocket once the bumper ring is off), bumper ring to the side rails (6, from inside the rail), bumper corner brackets (16). 2-1/2 in x 13: posts to rails (up through the rail and gusset)
Epoxy for the 16 glued frame joints (5-minute, any brand)

The tapered tenons on the filled LED corners (no cross screw: every way in for a screw head is a surface seen through the acrylic), and the one glued split across the gun well's front. Push a strip offcut through the tunnel across each joint while it cures
Hand riveter for 3/16 rivets, #11 drill, 120 deg countersink (stash)
Setting every bracket rivet; the countersink for the side plates, bottom corner gussets and bellypan
20x20 T-slot extrusion (your spares): 2 x 470 mm inside the gun well, 2 x 276 mm inside the gun's cradle plates, 2 x 372 mm across the front light bar hole

Gun well: one each side, flush with the towers' outboard face and 2 mm under the deck, one piece over the cut-down tower; the pivot's bearing block sits on it and the tower plate between it and the well-edge member. Gun: one inside each cradle plate along its top edge, flush with it. Front: flat on the frame's inner face behind the light bar hole, one along its bottom (the bar stands on it) and one along its top (free for sensors). All mirrored about the centreline and clear of the 0-90 deg swing; the cross holes in the in-well and front rails are a CNC side operation
Waterjet brackets: 1/8 in aluminium sheet (stash), 36 flat parts on the 12 x 12 waterjet

Nothing bent. Side plates (4: the Falcon and axle plates grown along the inner rail into every post: the rear ones take both sled posts, the tower and the rear tank post), inboard plates (6), arm knees (14), corner gussets (4 top, 4 bottom), tower plates (2) and rail spacer strips (2), (the bellypan is one CNC router piece now)
Bumper backing: 1x6 board (3/4 x 5-1/2 in actual), two 8 ft lengths (your call, 2026-11-06)

Four strips joined into one ring with printed corner brackets; 6 #10-32s through the side rails hold it and with them out it slides straight down. Replaces the 1/4 in plywood. Modelled in rev D.2. The ring sits 3/16 in off the chassis all round on printed spacers
